decisions.reason: After several years, the polymer concrete drain housing still fits the firm's core drainage engineering and system-family knowledge, so field experience can be absorbed and used to improve it rather than justify withdrawal.
The floor-level shower drainage system is central to the firm's customer base and future direction, giving it the strongest overlap with existing knowledge and the lowest likelihood of being dropped.
The shower element with integrated slope builds directly on the firm's installation, waterproofing, and integrated-system expertise, making continued refinement more attractive than exit.

Although less central than shower products, the backflow-protected basement floor drain remains a technically adjacent drainage solution that the firm can support and learn from with its existing engineering capabilities.

The air-admittance valve is the most peripheral to the firm's core shower and floor-drainage knowledge base, so strategic focus and weaker absorptive capacity make withdrawal the more likely decision.
